takeaway: The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior and runs superficially over it. Injury: no abduction above the horizontal and a winged scapula.

lines.text: An eighteen-year-old has a superficial stab wound on his right chest wall.
He cannot raise his right arm above the horizontal.
And when he presses his hands against a wall, his right scapula sticks out.
This is a winged scapula, from damage to the long thoracic nerve.
The long thoracic nerve supplies the serratus anterior muscle.
It runs superficially over the muscle, so it is vulnerable to injury.
Without serratus anterior, the glenoid cavity cannot rotate upwards.
So the damaged nerve is the long thoracic nerve.
